title: Spike: does WebRTC work phone-to-phone on the Orbic AP?
description: Gate for everything else. Tiny page (/room-test) that opens two data channels and reports ICE candidate types, connect time and round-trip ms. Check: AP client isolation, mDNS host candidates (Android Chrome hides LAN IPs behind .local names), whether any STUN is needed (none: LAN only, no internet), HTTPS cert trusted on both devices. Result decides WebRTC-direct vs box relay as the default transport.
notes:
Built (uncommitted): room.go (/api/room signaling+relay, tests in room_test.go), roomtest.html served at /room-test, scripts/dev/room-test.mjs (passes on loopback: direct 2 ms, via box 1 ms). Route wired in ui.go, /room-test in uiserver.go, /api/room excluded from the onion door. STILL TO DO: build+deploy, then open /room-test on two real phones on the Orbic AP and copy the report here.
RESULT 2026-10-10 (Pixel 6a <-> moto g 2025, both on the Orbic AP, no STUN): WebRTC works. Path host/host udp, 1 host candidate each, none hidden as .local. Connect 109 ms and 342 ms. Direct RTT median 42 ms (min 33-35, p95 50), 0 of 20 lost, both directions. Via-box measure is a self-echo (phone->box->phone) median 30-36 ms, NOT a true A->box->B relay, so it understates the relay: a real relay path is roughly two such round trips. Observation: ~40 ms is Wi-Fi hop latency (phones in power-save), fine for party games/remote input, marginal for twitch. FINDING: the Pixel's room WebSocket was found CLOSED (readyState 3) after sitting idle in a tab, so its room (CDWF) was gone and the Moto got 'no such room'. room.js (pf-ajt.3) must reconnect and re-join, and rooms should survive a short drop.
close_reason: WebRTC direct works between two phones on the Orbic AP; direct is the default transport, relay is fallback. See notes.

title: Room channel: survive dropped WebSocket (grace period, reconnect, resume id)
description: Spike found a phone's /api/room socket closed while its tab sat idle (Android Chrome freezes background tabs). Box should keep a room and peer slot for ~60 s after a socket drops; page should reconnect with the same peer id and re-negotiate only if the data channel died. Also measure a true A->box->B relay RTT, not a self-echo.
notes: Built: 60 s grace, id+token resume, away/back/leave events, pong, 90 s idle, client auto-reconnect with backoff and wake triggers, same-place on reload. Pending: real-phone check with the screen off for 1-2 minutes.

title: Page: room.js client library (join, peers, data channels, relay fallback)
description: Served like /bt/btclient.js. API: room.create(), room.join(code), onPeer, send(to|all, msg), on('msg'). Tries WebRTC data channel per peer, falls back to box relay when ICE fails in 4 s, reconnects on screen sleep. Unordered/unreliable channel option for game input, reliable for files. Heartbeat and presence.
notes: Built: roomclient/room.js (served /room/room.js), /room-test rebuilt on it. Headless test scripts/dev/room-test.mjs passes (27 checks) and fails when resume is broken on purpose. NOT yet run on the phones; close after that.

title: Box: room signaling and relay endpoint (/api/room WebSocket)
description: room.go, reusing wsAccept/wsRead/wsOriginOK from btbridge.go and the login gate in ui.go. JSON text frames: join{room,name,role}, peers, offer/answer/ice (addressed by peer id), relay{to,data} fallback, leave. In-memory only, nothing stored or logged. Limits: rooms, peers per room (8), message size (16 KB), rate per peer, idle timeout, shed on btLoadNow() like the bridge. Room codes 4 letters from an unambiguous alphabet, expire when empty. LAN-only path (add to onionPathOK exclusions). Tests like btmux_test.go.
close_reason: room.go: signaling, relay, grace period, resume tokens, limits; Go tests + Chromium test pass. Deploy and phone run still to do.

title: Shared room channel (signaling, room codes, QR)
description: WebRTC data channels with the box as signaling only (WebSocket rendezvous). Room code + QR join, presence, reconnect. Foundation for Fort Drop, Watch Party, Games. Open question: works with no internet? Check AP client isolation and mDNS ICE candidates on the Orbic first.

title: Room channel: tests (headless Chromium two-page test) and handoff docs
description: Extend scripts/dev with a two-page Chromium test (create, join, message both ways, relay fallback by blocking WebRTC, leave, room expiry). Add a Room section to docs/HANDOFF.md.

title: Join UX: room code, QR code, share link
description: Screen shows 4-letter code and a QR (small pure-JS QR encoder, no CDN). Phone joins via /room#CODE, remembers its name. Works inside /browse as a Room tab/sheet.

title: Kid mode and profiles
description: Per-device or per-profile mode: restricted tabs and ratings, hidden Web tab and Nyaa box, bedtime timer, PIN to leave. Box already knows devices and filter lists, so tie into devices.go and the DNS filter.

title: Audiobooks, podcasts and radio
description: Audio tab reusing the btclient audio.js player and service worker. Sources: LibriVox/Internet Archive audiobooks, podcast RSS, internet radio streams (probe CORS, add hosts to browseCSP). Resume position, speed control, sleep timer, background playback and media session controls.

title: Fort Drop: file and clipboard sharing between devices
description: AirDrop-style send of files, text and clipboard between devices on the fort. WebRTC data channel, chunked with progress, box is signaling only. Nothing stored on the box.

title: Browser game system (screen + phone controllers)
description: One browser is the console (authoritative game, canvas), phones are controllers (touch, DeviceMotion gyro, vibrate, Gamepad API) and private secondary screens (hands, hidden roles). Optional captureStream mirror to a second display. Start with 2-3 original party games; WASM emulator cores for homebrew/public domain later.

title: Comics and books reader (CBZ/EPUB)
description: In-page reader. Phase 1: open CBZ/EPUB from device (fflate unzip, blob URLs, preload next 2-3 pages, RTL, double page, long strip, remembered position, OPFS offline). Phase 2: fetch via existing WebTorrent path with want-file selection. Phase 3: AniList MANGA tab (same GraphQL endpoint). Sources: public domain and licensed only (Internet Archive, Digital Comic Museum, Standard Ebooks, Gutenberg). Probe CORS per source; add hosts to browseCSP.

title: Watch party: synced playback across screens
description: Host broadcasts play/pause/seek/time over the room channel; each device plays its own WebTorrent stream and corrects drift. Optional shared reactions.
